Name: Settle in at Stauffer
Description: Find a seat in one of the reading rooms, like the Alan G. Green Fireplace Reading Room, or grab a study pod on the ground floor. There's a Library Cafe on the main floor too.

Name: Browse the sci-fi lounge at Douglas
Description: Check out the Science Fiction & Fantasy Lounge and the Popular Science and New Books collections, or settle into a study carrel.

Name: Quiet study at Lederman Law
Description: Open to the entire Queen's community. Work in the large Reading Room or an upper-floor study carrel for quiet study.

Name: Unwind in Bracken's garden lounge
Description: Take a break in the Garden View Student Lounge on the main level, or work at the reading tables.

Name: Flip through YA books at Education
Description: Browse the children's and young adult book collection and current periodicals on the main floor of Duncan McArthur Hall.

Name: Study at Watson Hall LINQ
Description: A small learning space with 21 seats, open to all students, for studying solo or with friends.

Name: Shoot hoops at Open Rec Basketball
Description: Drop in to Open Recreation basketball at the ARC. No registration required; sign out equipment at a Q-Service Desk.

Name: Drop-in badminton at the ARC
Description: Drop in to Open Recreation badminton at the ARC. No registration required; sign out equipment at a Q-Service Desk.

Name: Recreational swim at the ARC pool
Description: Open recreational swim with the full pool available.

Name: Lane swim at the ARC pool
Description: Member lane swim in the shallow and deep ends.

Name: Coffee at the Library Cafe
Description: Grab a coffee or snack at the Library Cafe in Stauffer Library.

Name: Starbucks run at Mitchell Hall
Description: Pick up a drink at the Starbucks in Mitchell Hall.

Name: Tim Hortons at the Queen's Centre
Description: Grab a coffee and a snack at the Tim Hortons in the Queen's Centre.

Name: Smoothie at Booster Juice
Description: Pick up a smoothie or juice at Booster Juice in the Queen's Centre.

Name: Lunch break at Cafe Union
Description: Grab something to eat at Cafe Union in Goodes Hall, with halal and vegan options.

Name: Bite at Wally's
Description: Grab a bite at Wally's in Botterell Hall, with halal and vegan options.

Name: Walk to the pier
Description: Head down to the pier at Breakwater Park and look out over Lake Ontario.

Name: Music From Miles Around
Description: A free exhibition on Kingston's music history, with never-before-seen Tragically Hip artifacts and a jam space where you can pick up an instrument.
Place: Kingston City Hall, Market Wing Cultural Space

Name: Escape to the Safe Zone
Description: A solo exhibition by artist Leisa Rich: wall hangings, sculptures and installations of fantastical creatures exploring the fate of the natural world.

Name: Veterans Week Film Screening - Burd
Description: A screening of the award-winning documentary about Burdett "Burd" Sisler, one of Canada's last surviving WWII veterans, with director Abraam Dawod.

Name: Ingenuity Labs Presents: A Hard Day's Math: Connections between Mathematics and Music with Jason I. Brown (live music)
Description: Professor Jason I. Brown explores the connections between mathematics and music, with live musical accompaniment. Registration required.

Name: Canadian Foreign Policy at a Crossroads: Power, Purpose and Partnerships in a New Global Order with Jennifer Welsh
Description: The School of Policy Studies' 2026 J. Douglas Gibson Lecture, given by Jennifer M. Welsh of McGill University.

Name: Hyprov featuring Colin Mochrie and Asad Mecci
Description: Improv legend Colin Mochrie and hypnotist Asad Mecci team up, with hypnotized audience volunteers joining the improvisers on stage.

Name: Gem and Mineral Sale at the Miller Museum
Description: Browse cut gemstones, natural minerals, crystals and fossils for sale from two local businesses owned by Queen's geology alumni.

Name: Service of Remembrance
Description: A Service of Remembrance honouring Canadian soldiers and the Queen's students, alumni, faculty and staff who lost their lives in service.

Name: Think Grad Studies Panel Discussion with Current Students
Description: Current Arts and Science grad students talk about why to consider grad school and how it differs from undergrad. Registration required.

Name: Open Mic at The Buckle hosted by Lukas Oak
Description: Perform or just watch at the every-other-Wednesday open mic hosted by Lukas Oak. No cover.

Name: Why Is It So Hard to Get Inclusion of People with Disabilities Effectively Embedded in the Policy Development Process?
Description: David Lepofsky speaks on why it is so hard to get the inclusion of people with disabilities built into policy development.

Name: Matthew Good and His Band featuring Kevin Fox and His String Quartet
Description: Two 45-minute sets of hits, deep cuts and rare B-sides, played with a string quartet led by cellist Kevin Fox.

Name: Hockey Helps the Homeless
Description: A charity hockey event at the Invista Centre raising money for local homelessness organizations.

Name: Youth Imagine The Future Exhibition of Writing & Art
Description: An exhibition of eco-art and solarpunk short stories by local teens imagining futures built on real climate solutions.

Name: Care and Migration in Context of Climate Change: Using Mongolia as a Case Study with Dr. Ito Peng
Description: A Political Studies colloquium on climate-driven rural-to-urban migration and care in Mongolia, based on over 100 interviews.

Name: Live Music on the Belvedere Patio
Description: Local artist Taryn McKenna plays one of the last live music sessions of the season on the Belvedere Hotel patio.

Name: Festive Friday @ Skandiflow
Description: Browse handmade skincare, soaps and jewellery during Downtown Kingston's Festive Friday, with live harp, piano and vocals by Malobi and $5 mocktails.

Name: Distinguished Service Award (DSA) celebration
Description: A reception honouring the 2026 Distinguished Service Award recipients. Tickets are $20 for students, plus HST and fees.
Place: Isabel Bader Centre for the Performing Arts

Name: Sophie's Surprise 29th
Description: A '90s-themed party show of circus, acrobatics and comedy with performers from Cirque du Soleil, La Clique and The 7 Fingers.

Name: Jeff Leeson: Only Gonna Say This Once Comedy Tour
Description: Stand-up comedy from internationally touring comedian Jeff Leeson.

Name: Friday Nights in the Recital Hall: Bageshree Vaze and Vineet Vyas
Description: Kathak and Bharatanatyam dancer and vocalist Bageshree Vaze and tabla artist Vineet Vyas bring North Indian classical dance and music to life. Tickets $25.
Place: Isabel Bader Centre for the Performing Arts

Name: Stephen Stanley & NoElectric with Jennifer Foster
Description: A campfire-style concert with Stephen Stanley, a founding member of The Lowest of the Low. On Wolfe Island, so you'll need the ferry.

Name: The Ultimate Card Show
Description: Browse vendor tables of sports cards, Pokémon and other trading card games and collectibles.

Name: 4th Annual KSS Holiday Bazaar
Description: Over 75 vendors, a silent auction, a raffle and the KSS Cafe at Kingston Secondary School. $2 at the door.

Name: The Jury Experience – The Killer AI
Description: An interactive courtroom drama where the audience is the jury: hear the testimony, weigh the evidence and vote on the verdict.

Name: Dark Matter Day: Observatory Tour and Science Talk with Prof. Kyle Leach
Description: Prof. Kyle Leach talks about the search for dark matter, followed by a tour of the Queen's Observatory.

Name: The Great Canadian Roadtrip with Doc Walker, Michelle Wright and Jason McCoy
Description: Canadian country stars Doc Walker, Michelle Wright and Jason McCoy share one stage.

Name: Sam Polley and the Old Tomorrows
Description: Vintage rockabilly from Toronto band Sam Polley and the Old Tomorrows. On Wolfe Island, so you'll need the ferry.

Name: Selina Martin LIVE!
Description: Canadian singer-songwriter Selina Martin plays raw, high-energy rock. On Wolfe Island, so you'll need the ferry.

Name: Jan Lisiecki in Concert
Description: Canadian pianist Jan Lisiecki performs dance-inspired works by Chopin, Brahms and Bartók. Tickets $70-$75.
Place: Isabel Bader Centre for the Performing Arts

Name: Displacement, Home and Belonging in "Fatherland" – Screening & History Talk with Dr. Swen Steinberg
Description: A screening of Paweł Pawlikowski's Fatherland, about Thomas Mann's return to postwar Germany, followed by a history talk. Tickets required.

Name: FLSQ Speaker Rachel Rebouché
Description: Rachel Rebouché talks about how abortion access in the U.S. has come to depend on travel since the Dobbs decision. Registration required.

Name: Think Grad Studies Panel Discussion with Current Students
Description: Current Arts and Science grad students talk about why to consider grad school and how it differs from undergrad. Registration required.

Name: Inner Harbour Jazz Trio
Description: Blue Note-inspired jazz with organ, drums, guitar and vocals: swing, blues, hard bop and classic standards.

Name: All You Can Eat Pasta Night!
Description: Two kinds of fresh pasta with bolognese and pomodoro sauces, plus bread, salad and sweets. Reservations highly recommended.

Name: Queen's Health Sciences Graduate Program Open House
Description: Talk one-on-one with reps and current students from graduate programs in Medicine, Nursing and Rehabilitation.

Name: Miigis: Underwater Panther – A Red Sky Performance production
Description: A contemporary Indigenous dance work inspired by the Anishinaabe journey from the Atlantic Ocean to the Great Lakes. Pay what you want.

Name: Celebrate Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Day in the Library
Description: Drop in to explore geospatial resources and connect with others interested in maps and data. Everyone is welcome.

Name: Research Unlocked: Navigating the Copyright Legalities of Training and Using AI
Description: Copyright Librarian Meaghan Shannon covers the copyright questions raised by training and using generative AI. Open to undergrads. Registration required.

Name: International Education Week Panel and Soup Lunch
Description: A free soup lunch and student panel for International Education Week, open to the whole Queen's community.

Name: Queen's Graduate Roundtables on Global Challenges - Sustainable Cities
Description: Queen's graduate researchers discuss how to create just and sustainable cities.

Name: Trooper
Description: Juno-winning Canadian rock band Trooper, inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame in 2023.

Name: Whiskey Smoke Duo
Description: Acoustic favourites from Whiskey Smoke Duo at The Buckle, every other Wednesday.

Name: Kingston Potters' Guild Holiday Sale
Description: Browse and buy handmade ceramics by Kingston Potters' Guild members in the Tett Centre's Malting Tower.

Name: 2026 Metal Rocks Holiday Show & Sale
Description: Handcrafted jewellery, natural minerals, crystals and polished gemstones from the Kingston Lapidary & Mineral Club.

Name: Book Launch: Reclaiming Canadian Sovereignty in a Ruptured World with Bob Rae
Description: Bob Rae launches Reclaiming Canadian Sovereignty in a Ruptured World, a book bringing together twenty Canadian voices on Canada in a changing world.

Name: The Truth In Reconciliation: A Conversation, Part 1
Description: Part 1 of a four-part conversation on Queen's progress on reconciliation, with Te ho wis kwûnt, Al Doxtator, and Principal Patrick Deane. Registration required.

Name: Meisel Lecture: How to Elbow Up for Phase Out? Canada and the Global Imperative to End Oil Production, Dr. Angela Carter
Description: Dr. Angela Carter gives the annual John Meisel Lecture on Canada and the global push to end oil production. Registration required.

Name: Basia Bulat
Description: Three-time Polaris Prize finalist Basia Bulat performs her mix of folk, soul and gospel.

Name: SULLY BURROWS, Bradley Hale, and Abby Stewart
Description: SULLY BURROWS plays live at the Broom Factory with support from Bradley Hale and Abby Stewart.

Name: Dear Evan Hansen
Description: The Kingston Meistersingers perform the six-time Tony Award-winning musical. Student tickets $30.

Name: Live Music on the Belvedere Patio
Description: Local artist Vince Stabile plays one of the last live music sessions of the season on the Belvedere Hotel patio.

Name: Fight For a Cause
Description: Sanctioned charity boxing with student fighters from Queen's, Western and McGill, raising money for Jack.org.
Place: DoubleTree by Hilton, Ambassador Event Centre

Name: Crown Lands with Dreamland
Description: Crown Lands plays a standing-room show at the Broom Factory with support from Dreamland. All ages.

Name: K is for Kingston, K is for Katarokwi book launch
Description: The launch of a new Kingston book, with a reading, live music by Anna Sudac and Christina Foster, and a chance to meet the creators.
Place: Kingston Frontenac Public Library, Central Branch

Name: A Festive Celebration
Description: A candlelit holiday concert featuring Ola Gjeilo's Dreamweaver and harpist Caroline Leonardelli. Student tickets $15.
Place: Isabel Bader Centre for the Performing Arts

Name: Castagnata Christmas Market
Description: A Christmas market with local vendors, free hot cocoa, coffee and tea, carolling, and roasted chestnuts for sale from 1 to 3 pm.

Name: Alan Cross
Description: Alan Cross presents Uncharted live at the Broom Factory. Seated, all ages.

Name: Kingston Choral Society presents "The Heart of Winter; A Choral Advent"
Description: An Advent choral concert by the Kingston Choral Society. Student tickets $16 + HST.

Name: The Velveteen Rabbit
Description: A modern-day retelling of The Velveteen Rabbit by Rule of Three Theatre, with singing and dancing.

Name: Play Shipwrights by Improbable Escapes
Description: A one-hour escape room about Kingston's historic shipbuilders, at easy-to-medium difficulty, for groups of 2 to 6.

Name: Great Lakes Museum Exhibitions
Description: See the history of the Great Lakes up close, from the S.S. Keewatin to Kingston's naval heritage.

Name: Military Communications and Electronics Museum
Description: Over 20,000 square feet of galleries on the history of military communications and electronics in Canada.

Name: Classic Kingston Food Tour
Description: A guided walking tour of historic downtown Kingston with tastings at local restaurants. $89 under 19, $99 for 19+.
Place: Starts at the Visitor Information Centre, 209 Ontario St

Name: Board Games at Spearhead
Description: Tacos, beer and board games every Tuesday at Spearhead Brewing. No cover.

Name: Board Games at Something in the Water
Description: Board games every Wednesday at Something in the Water Brewing. No cover.
Place: Something in the Water Brewing Co.

Name: Original Thursdays at The Cove Inn
Description: Live original music from local songwriters every Thursday. By donation. In Westport, outside Kingston.

Name: Kingston Nerd Night
Description: A volunteer-run weekly game night with a big board game library, trading card games and regular D&D sessions. You can bring your own games too.

Name: Trivia At Daft Brewing
Description: Weekly team trivia with image and music rounds and $100 in prizes. Teams of up to 6.

Name: Board Games at One Eyed Jack
Description: Strategy, co-op and party games provided by The Board Bartender. No cover.

Name: Trivia Games at One Eyed Jack
Description: Trivia and other brain-buster games over dinner and drinks, run by The Board Bartender. No cover.

Name: Karaoke at The Buckle
Description: Weekly karaoke night where everyone is welcome to take the stage.

Name: Weekly Karaoke at Daft
Description: Karaoke every Friday from 9 pm to 2 am, hosted by AADJs.
